headline: Semantic Kernel can ingest Perplexity outputs via MCP/plugins, creating medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct filesystem overlap is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG agent that ingests uploaded documents and browsing context, while Semantic Kernel can connect to MCP servers and OpenAPI tools. That creates a plausible path where Perplexity-generated content is fed into SK as trusted input. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Perplexity output through an MCP tool or plugin without provenance tagging, injection risk is present.
IF Perplexity content is copied into SK prompts or memory as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Perplexity outputs before SK ingests them.
Disable automatic tool execution on retrieved text in SK.
Require a human review step for any Perplexity-derived instruction.
Use a fixed prompt template that treats retrieved text as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and provenance filters in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, and Semantic Kernel reads files and can send data to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face or MCP servers. If the same workspace or memory store is used, sensitive document content can flow from A into B’s outbound API calls. The profiles do not show isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or memory store, file contents can flow from Perplexity into Semantic Kernel.
IF Semantic Kernel forwards retrieved file text to a model provider or MCP server, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Restrict SK to a read-only subset of files.
Turn off automatic file ingestion in SK for shared folders.
Review outbound destinations for any Perplexity-derived content.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity cannot write the host filesystem, but Semantic Kernel can read and write files and use MCP. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite or reinterpret artifacts that A produced or that A’s users expect to remain stable. The conflict is not guaranteed, but the overlap is real enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same directory, write conflicts are possible.
IF Semantic Kernel uses MCP tools that mutate shared resources, conflicts can occur even without shell access.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Make SK write to a staging folder only.
Use file locks or atomic rename conventions.
Disable write access for SK on shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live search, and Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as plugin inputs or agent context. If SK accepts Perplexity answers without verification, factual errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated content. The pair’s interaction is plausible by design, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Perplexity answers as authoritative context without verification, cascading error risk exists.
IF SK triggers downstream actions from Perplexity-derived facts, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require source verification before SK acts on Perplexity output.
Keep Perplexity as a suggestion-only source.
Log and diff upstream claims before execution.
Add a second retrieval source for cross-checking.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating in the orchestrator.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and touches uploaded documents, while Semantic Kernel is a library that can route data to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers and handle provider keys. If regulated or residency-bound data is passed through SK into those services, policy mismatch can occur. The profiles do not prove a violation, but they do show a plausible compliance boundary.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Semantic Kernel to a provider lacking the required residency or retention terms, compliance risk exists.
IF Perplexity uploads contain restricted data and SK forwards them to third-party APIs, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Block regulated data from SK outbound tools.
Confirm provider DPAs and residency settings.
Limit Perplexity uploads to non-sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing in the orchestrator.
